title: Abu Ubaydah
hookLine: called the trustworthy one of this community (Bukhari)

cards: Visitors from Najran come to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, with a request: send someone back with us, someone trustworthy. He answers: I will send you a man who is truly trustworthy, truly.
In the room, people sit up. The report in Sahih al-Bukhari says the companions each hoped it would be them. Then he says: stand up, Abu Ubaydah.
Today: the man the Prophet picked when the job was simply to be trusted.

teach.b: His full name was Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and his story turns on one word.
Bukhari records the Prophet saying: every community has its amin, its trustworthy one, and the amin of this community is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah.

teach.h: THE ONE WITH WHOM THINGS ARE SAFE.
teach.b: To be amin is to be the person with whom things are safe: a deposit, a secret, a decision, a town far away that you're sent to serve. It's a strange kind of praise.
Courage shows up on a battlefield; generosity shows up in a gift.
Trustworthiness mostly shows up as nothing happening. The money is all there, the promise is kept, the secret stays secret, and nobody notices.

Later, Bukhari places Abu Ubaydah among the commanders in Syria who rode out to meet the caliph Umar when plague broke out there. Umar decided to turn back. Abu Ubaydah asked him: are you running from God's decree?
Umar answered: yes, we run from God's decree to God's decree.

Trust doesn't mean always agreeing. It means you can say the hard thing to a friend and still be trusted. The man sent to Najran was the same man who would stand in Syria and put a hard question to the caliph.

how: Muslims treat amanah, a trust, as a serious religious duty: deposits, promises, secrets and responsibilities are held as trusts, and Abu Ubaydah's title is one example teachers give.

o: the general who led the army at the battle of Badr
the scribe who wrote the treaty sent to Najran
the companion the Prophet named this community's amin

p: the one with whom things are safe

s: the Prophet said every community has its trustworthy one
and that the amin of this community is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah.
the companions hoped to be the one chosen for Najran
Bukhari says each hoped it would be him; it was Abu Ubaydah.
being trustworthy meant Abu Ubaydah never disagreed with Umar
he asked Umar: are you running from God's decree? trust and honesty went together.

games.q: you're a companion in the room. the Prophet says he will send a truly trustworthy man to Najran. what goes through your mind?
o: hope that it will be you.
certainty that it will be you.
games.why: the report says the companions each hoped to be chosen. then he said: stand up, Abu Ubaydah.

practice: Look at what's been handed to you lately: a friend's secret, a borrowed book, a small promise like I'll call you at six.
Pick the one most likely to slip, and settle in your mind exactly how it will be kept, quietly, with no announcement. If you pray, you can ask to be someone with whom things are safe.

wordCard.voice: Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. The companion the Prophet called the amin, the trustworthy one, of this community, and the one he sent when a people asked for someone they could trust. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: trustworthy, the one with whom things are safe; the title the Prophet gave Abu Ubaydah.

carryVoice: Your line: trustworthy of the ummah. Trust mostly looks like nothing happening. Rest well.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3744 (every community has its amin; the amin of this community is Abu Ubaydah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4380–4381 (Najran asks for a trustworthy man; the companions hoped; Abu Ubaydah sent)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5729 (plague in Syria; Abu Ubaydah: are you running from God's decree?; Umar: from God's decree to God's decree)
